correspondence.component_scope: mainstem_chosen_opening
correspondence.finding: The eastern selected mainstem opening is in the mapped upper Tye River valley. The labelled channel runs west and then southwest beside the Stevens Pass highway corridor into the lower Tye valley. The selected start is treated as a chosen river-valley opening, not asserted to be the natural source.

correspondence.component_scope: tye_foss_south_fork_transition
correspondence.finding: The source depicts Tye River meeting the northward Foss River and the resulting westward South Fork Skykomish corridor. The selected mainstem continues along this connected valley past the Skykomish area, with the Beckler and Miller approaches visible. These are distinct reach names within the representative receiving system.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Tye River–Foss River junction and South Fork Skykomish River

correspondence.component_scope: skykomish_forks_and_middle_corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected South Fork route reaches the mapped North Fork junction in the Index/Heybrook area and continues as labelled Skykomish River. Overlapping original views establish the downstream valley, Wallace/Sultan surroundings, Sultan and Monroe reaches without a missing selected through-link.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: South Fork Skykomish–North Fork Skykomish junction and Skykomish River

correspondence.component_scope: tributary_chosen_opening
correspondence.finding: The southern tributary begins within the mapped upper Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley near Iron Cap Mountain and continues southwest along the named channel. Nearby alpine lakes and Hinman Glacier are outside the selected opening; no lake crossing or glacier traversal is needed to establish this selected river-valley passage. The natural source point and current glacier extent are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: middle_fork_valley
correspondence.finding: The selected tributary follows the continuously depicted Middle Fork through the Burntboot/Dingford Creek surroundings, the westward bend toward the Taylor River junction, and the lower valley past the Pratt River junction toward North Bend. The nearby lakes belong to adjacent tributary settings; they are not imposed as through-lakes on the selected line.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Middle Fork Snoqualmie River through its upper and middle valley

correspondence.component_scope: snoqualmie_fork_junctions
correspondence.finding: The western Middle Fork approach and the adjoining North Fork/South Fork confluence area near North Bend and Snoqualmie are depicted with connected river linework. The selected route continues northwest into the labelled Snoqualmie River corridor. No one scalar hydronym is assigned to all these named forks.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Middle Fork and the Snoqualmie fork-junction area

correspondence.component_scope: snoqualmie_falls_passage
correspondence.finding: The selected river passes the explicitly labelled Snoqualmie Falls setting and continues downstream toward Fall City and the Raging River junction. The map establishes the ordinary above-falls to below-falls geographic passage. No contemporary facility operation, diversion proportion, discharge or exact engineered channel is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_snoqualmie_tributary
correspondence.finding: The selected tributary continues along the labelled Snoqualmie River past the Tolt junction and Carnation, then Duvall and the lower floodplain to its Skykomish joining area. Horseshoe Lake and other floodplain waterbodies are mapped alongside the river; the selected through-route is the river corridor rather than a separate lake-to-lake transfer.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Snoqualmie River through Carnation and Duvall

correspondence.component_scope: shared_confluence_and_fragment_join
correspondence.finding: Independent original linework depicts Snoqualmie joining Skykomish west of Monroe and the combined downstream river continuing northwest as Snohomish River. This covers the actual inter-fragment/tributary junction at ordinary confluence scale. The end of tributary 9446 is this joining area, not the coastal terminal. Generalized selected positions are not used to assign a precise confluence vertex.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Skykomish–Snoqualmie confluence and Snohomish River beginning

correspondence.component_scope: snohomish_lower_river
correspondence.finding: The selected downstream mainstem follows the continuously mapped Snohomish River through the city of Snohomish and around the broad lower floodplain to Everett. Overlapping clean views show the Pilchuck joining area and the river/slough network around Ebey Island. The selected corridor remains the mapped river course; adjacent floodplain lakes do not create an unestablished through-lake passage.

correspondence.component_scope: actual_selected_terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected final mainstem approaches Everett along the labelled Snohomish River west of the principal delta islands and reaches its mapped mouth/Port Gardner setting at Preston Point. The surrounding Union, Steamboat and Ebey slough branches are visible and are distinguished from the selected terminal corridor. The simplified endpoint is not asserted as an exact present river mouth or bank intersection.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Snohomish River mouth at the Preston Point–Port Gardner setting

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southeastern opening and first westward/northwestward chain, including the joins among these four selected parts.
correspondence.finding: The regional hydrology chapter gives karst context but no locality-level identification of this opening or a connected surface route through the initial parts. No named headwater or selected cenote connection is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward inland continuation and its joins with the opening and central chain.
correspondence.finding: No acquired source depicts or describes a through-channel along these selected inland parts. General groundwater movement does not assign a river name or establish these particular connections.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward continuation, short intervening parts, northwestward bends and entry to the northern leg.
correspondence.finding: The retained chapters contain no corridor map identifying these selected bends or their intervening joins. Nearby lagoon names and the regional aquifer setting do not settle this western inland correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward inland leg and its northwestward approach toward the coast.
correspondence.finding: The CICY synthesis explains a regional setting in which groundwater can emerge at the coast. It does not identify a surface-water corridor linking these selected parts to the coastal zone, and the acquired field map has no coverage of this inland leg.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastward final coastal approach before the last selected part.
correspondence.finding: Carbonera is an independently documented lagoon in the northern coastal setting. The narrow field-site map does not cover this selected approach or establish its joins through intervening wetlands. No particular canal, managed crossing or spring connection is assigned to the selected chain.

correspondence.component_scope: Last northward coastal part and its actual endpoint, without replacing it with a nearby documented lagoon mouth.
correspondence.finding: Figure1 depicts a small Carbonera mouth-area sampling channel. Its regional locator and narrow local panel do not establish the selected last part, barrier crossing or actual endpoint as that channel. The documented lagoon opening is retained only as a contextual feature; no Gulf outlet correspondence is claimed for the selected terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected eastern opening and initial feeder
correspondence.finding: Figure2-1 depicts the chosen eastern mountain-side opening in a connected quebrada that descends southwest and west to the broad bend feeding the upper Pedernales corridor. No separate initial-feeder label is established. This is a mapped through-link, not merely basin membership.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper bend and Quebrada Pedernales
correspondence.finding: The map shows the selected northwesterly tributary corridor into the named Pedernales reach, its westward bend and turn toward Pelícano. The nearby El Tabaco branch remains distinct and is not substituted for the selected feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Quebrada Pelícano and Tres Cruces junction
correspondence.finding: The selected course continues south through the mapped Pelícano valley to its junction with the east-arriving Los Choros corridor at Tres Cruces. Printed p24 independently describes the Pelícano contribution from the north at Tres Cruces.

correspondence.component_scope: Tres Cruces through Punta Colorada and El Trapiche
correspondence.finding: Own Figure2-1 continuously depicts the westbound main valley through the settlement and tributary-join setting. Printed p24 distinguishes the lateral contributions and the lower Choros Altos/La Higuera tributary. Road lines are distinguished from the blue hydrographic course by the legend.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Los Choros alluvial corridor and lateral joins
correspondence.finding: The selected lower west/northwest bends follow the mapped Los Choros course, including lower tributary approaches. The mapped channel corridor and the report drainage account support passage through the sediment-filled valley; no exact bank or present flow is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal approach and coastal outlet
correspondence.finding: The map follows the final westward reach, lower Romero junction setting and final coastal approach to the Pacific outlet. The selected terminal lies in that depicted outlet corridor. This is corridor-scale mouth correspondence, not a contemporary shoreline or open-water-flow claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake, reservoir, managed and alluvial passages
correspondence.finding: No lake or reservoir interrupts the selected course on the inspected map. Printed p40 reports no reservoir, canal or major irrigation infrastructure identified in the study basin. Printed p24 describes lateral alluvial cones merging with main-valley sediments and generally dry channels outside unusually wet years. The finding concerns the natural mapped drainage corridor; it does not claim current operations or perennial hydraulic continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and unnamed southwestern Sierra La Paila feeder
correspondence.finding: The Ramos Arizpe relief map shows the selected small westward-to-southwestward opening and its successive foothill bends on the southwestern side of Sierra La Paila. This initial feeder is unnamed on the inspected map. Its ordinary corridor position and approach to the western foothill trunk are supported without assigning an exact surveyed source vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Western Arroyo El Carmen join and southward foothill descent
correspondence.finding: The opening joins the western foothill watercourse labeled Arroyo El Carmen. The consecutive southward passage along the Parras boundary and southwestward departure into the plain correspond on the adjoining Ramos Arizpe and Parras maps. The independently drawn eastern El Carmen approach is not substituted for this western selected route. No precise name-change point is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Arroyo Grande Las Liebres westward plain corridor
correspondence.finding: The Parras relief map directly labels the selected westward and then northwestward plain watercourse Arroyo Grande Las Liebres. Its successive foothill-side tributary joins and approach to the San Pedro boundary are visible. Presa La Tapada and Presa Tanque Las Liebres are separately mapped local waterbodies; the selected route is not assigned an unproved crossing of either. Arroyo Mezquite Verde is a separately drawn, more southerly neighboring course.

correspondence.component_scope: San Pedro entry and westward northern arc
correspondence.finding: The maps establish the Parras–San Pedro boundary setting and the adjoining streams, but do not establish a continuously connected watercourse along the entire selected westward arc. The San Pedro original labels nearby Arroyo Mezquite Verde and depicts several separate incoming channels. Their presence does not establish the selected transverse link or justify transferring that name.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern traverse near Presa Mala Noche and Cerro Los Indios
correspondence.finding: The San Pedro relief map identifies Presa Mala Noche, Cerro Los Indios and the neighboring Arroyo La Barranca drainage. Those anchors locate the selected lower corridor, but its specific westward-to-southwestward connections across the mapped plain/channel network are not established. A selected reservoir passage, diversion or other managed connection is not inferred from the nearby reservoir label.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northern Parras plain branch and actual inland terminal
correspondence.finding: The final part returns into the northern Parras plain north of Cerro La Casita. The Parras map depicts an unnamed small north–south stream segment at the final-tip surroundings. This supports the local endpoint setting, but the incoming selected connection from the San Pedro traverse is not established for the complete final part. No named lake crossing or receiving mouth is shown at the actual selected ending, and it is not extended to Laguna de Mayrán or to Río Nazas.
